document.abstract: File-based production workflows, especially time-critical news contributions, suffer from long data transfer times when files need to be exchanged over wide area networks (WAN). On one hand, standard tools like the file transfer protocol (FTP) are based on the transmission control protocol and suffer massively from WAN characteristics. On the other hand, typical WAN file transfer acceleration solutions require installation of additional proprietary software, resulting in changed workflows with significant user impact and integration effort. To compensate for these drawbacks, a novel approach for accelerating workflows without any user impact and virtually zero integration effort has been implemented and is introduced here. Different FTP-based transfer scenarios will be analyzed with a focus on the end-to-end performance gain. — Detailed results from a real-life scenario involving an international news contribution for a public broadcaster will be presented and reveal significant performance gain on the involved 8 Mbit/sec WAN link as well as on multi-gigabit links, without adapting or replacing the established production system.

authors.bio: Ralf Einhorn has a professional background in research and development with a strong focus on distributed network services and infrastructures. He has worked on service-oriented architectures, web technologies, storage systems, and network supported A/V technologies. — As senior R&D engineer in the production workflow lab at Thomson/Technicolor Corporate Research Einhorn was responsible for the IT-based distributed movie production testbed and worked on various international projects. He took a major role in designing architectures for system integration of interactive multimedia applications in virtualized environments. — Einhorn studied electrical engineering and computer science at the TU Braunschweig and the University of Hannover. He earned a Ph.D. (Dr.-Ing.) at the Institute for Computer Networks and Distributed systems at the Computing Centre Lower Saxony and at the L3S Research Centre. Einhorn is co-founder and CEO of TIXEL, a company focused on high-performance data transfer in wide area IP networks.
authors.name: R. Einhorn

authors.bio: Andreas Aust is currently chief technical officer at TIXEL and has more than 17 years of experience in developing, designing, and architecting software systems for a variety of media related projects covering signal processing for audio codecs, mobile entertainment platforms, scalable software frameworks, and optimized network protocol stacks. — Since 2005, Aust has focused on high-performance network applications and service-oriented architectures. He has managed many research projects and holds several media and IT-related patents. — Aust studied electrical engineering at the RWTH Aachen, where he earned an engineering degree (Dipl.-Ing.) in 1996. From 1996 to 2009, he held various positions at Thomson/Technicolor. He was part of the incubator team from 2001 to 2004, starting a new U.S. Research Lab in Princeton. Aust co-founded TIXEL in 2009.
authors.name: A. Aust

authors.bio: Lars Fürst studied at The Technical University of Dortmund, Germany, where he earned a degree (Dipl.-Ing.) in Information Technology Engineering from the Institute of Robotics and Information Technology. During his study, he focused on digital A/V signal processing, communication engineering, and software development. — After graduation, Fürst started his professional career as a R&D engineer in the production workflow lab at Thomson/Technicolor Corporate Research. His research was focused on service-oriented architectures for realtime media production workflows, distributed storage architectures and file systems. After five successful years with Thomson/Technicolor, Fürst joined a team of engineers at TIXEL. He has been responsible for software product development of high-performance data transfer solutions, standardization, as well as pre-sales and is currently in charge of TIXEL's business development.
authors.name: L. E. Furst

authors.bio: Michael Wittmann studied electrical engineering with an emphasis on psychoacoustics and cybernetics at the Technical University Munich (TUM). He is co-founder and chief technology officer of David Systems and has profound knowledge in signal processing, audio electronics and software development. Founded in 1991, DAVID Systems is a pioneer in offering end-to-end software-based solutions to enable tapeless workflows in radio, television, and rich media broadcast applications. David Systems has a history of experience in CMS/MAM-based media exchange and delivers integrated solutions, which scale from a single mobile device (media upload for journalist) to multi organization media exchange (ARD-File exchange for news, music and video).
authors.name: M. Wittmann
